prompt.spec:
## CRM lead API
- Full reference (generated live; read it first if you have web access): {{docsUrl}}
- Endpoint: POST {{endpoint}}
- Headers:
  Content-Type: application/json
  {{keyLine}}
- Body fields (JSON):
  - source (required, string): lead source, e.g. "Website form", "Baidu ads"
  - name (required, string): customer name
  - contactInfo (required, string): phone, WeChat or email
  - intendedServices (optional, string array): services of interest. Allowed values: {{services}}. Values not in the list are recorded as {{fallback}} with the original value added to notes
  - notes (optional, string): notes
  - adInfo (optional, object): ad tracking info with keys ip, url, 账户 (account), 广告计划 (campaign), 广告组 (ad group), 广告 (ad)
  - crm_vid (optional, string): once the website uses visitor tracking, forms carry a hidden crm_vid field (visitor ID); pass it through as is to link the visitor's source
  - Any other fields are accepted and appended to notes
- Success: HTTP 201 with {"data":{"id":"lead id","status":"New"}}; if a lead with the same contact already exists within 30 days, HTTP 200 with {"data":{"id":"existing lead id","duplicate":true}} means it was merged into that lead, which also counts as success
- Errors: 401 missing or invalid key; 400 invalid parameters (e.g. a required field is missing), the body says which field
- CORS is allowed, but the key must never be exposed to browsers

req.website:
## Requirements
1. The key must not appear in front-end code. The form should post to our own back end (or a cloud/edge function), which adds the key and forwards the request to the CRM.
2. Map the form fields to the fields above; make source identify the page; put the landing page url, visitor ip and ad parameters from the URL into adInfo where possible; if the form has a hidden crm_vid field, pass it to the CRM unchanged.
3. If the CRM call fails, do not change what the visitor sees; just log it on the back end.
req.webhook:
## Requirements
1. Ad platforms usually cannot send custom headers, so use a relay (e.g. a Cloudflare Worker or cloud function) that receives the platform push, verifies the platform signature and forwards it to the CRM.
2. Map the platform fields to the fields above: source is the platform name; account, campaign, ad group and ad go into adInfo.
3. Return the success response the platform expects; when the CRM returns an error, log it and rely on the platform's retry mechanism if needed.
req.generic:
## Requirements
1. First understand the structure of our existing system, pick the most suitable integration point, and tell me your plan.
2. Keep the key only in server-side environment variables.
3. If a field mapping is unclear, ask me instead of guessing.

prompt.verify:
## Verification
1. Debug with a dry run first: add ?dryRun=1 to the endpoint. The API only validates and returns the normalized result without creating a lead. Make sure the field mapping is right.
2. Finally send one real test lead with source "Integration test" and confirm it returns 201 (submitting the same contact again within 30 days returns 200 with duplicate:true, meaning it was merged). Then tell me the test lead's ID so I can delete it in the CRM.

script.place: Add this line before </head> on every page (once in the shared layout or template; in index.html for single-page apps):

intro.title: Workflow Automation
intro.subtitle: Understand how workflows run, trigger conditions, and execution flow
intro.body: Workflows automatically execute a series of actions when specific conditions are met, reducing manual work and ensuring consistent business processes. You can configure and enable workflows in System settings → AI & automation.

trigger.title: Trigger
trigger.desc: Entity created, or field changed to a specified value

match.title: Match
match.desc: Find all enabled workflows and check each trigger condition

execute.title: Execute
execute.desc: Run actions in order; earlier results are available to later template variables

onCreate.label: On Create
onCreate.desc: Fires immediately when an entity (lead/client) is created. Good for welcome notifications or initializing default field values.

fieldChange.label: Field Change
fieldChange.desc: Fires when a specified field changes to a particular value, e.g. Status → Confirmed, or Owner → Any. Supports 'Any' to fire on any change.

scheduled.label: Scheduled
scheduled.desc: Auto-scans all records daily at 09:00 (Asia/Shanghai) and executes actions on matching entities. Supports: date field = today, date field expired, no activity for N days.

intro.asyncDescPre: All workflow actions run asynchronously in the background (fire-and-forget) and do not block the frontend response.
intro.asyncDescPost: action's database writes happen in real time, but you need to refresh the page to see the updated values.

vars.subtitle: Dynamically reference entity data and time in emails, webhooks, and field assignments
vars.unrecognizedPost: (not replaced with empty), making configuration errors easy to spot.
vars.timeNote: Time variables are calculated based on the timezone in system settings (default Asia/Shanghai). Week starts on Monday; month follows the calendar month.
vars.leadNotePost: come from the linked user table; other fields are read directly from the lead record.
vars.clientNotePost: come from the linked user table.

actionsSection.title: Action Types
actionsSection.subtitle: Five actions available after a workflow triggers, with configuration guides

set_field.label: Auto Set Field
set_field.desc: Automatically set a field to a specified value when trigger conditions are met. Field values support template variables.
notes: Actions execute in list order; a previous action's result is immediately available to subsequent template variables
Field values can use template variables such as {{today}}, {{name}}, etc.

send_email.label: Send Email
send_email.desc: Send a notification email to specified recipients on trigger. Recipients, subject, and body all support template variables.
notes: Email is sent via SendGrid; configure SENDGRID_API_KEY in Cloudflare Workers environment variables
Recipient can be a fixed address or dynamic via {{assignedToEmail}} / {{assignedSalesEmail}}
Body is plain text; line breaks are preserved

webhook.label: Webhook
webhook.desc: Send an HTTP request to an external system on trigger. URL and body both support template variables.
notes: Body should be valid JSON; string values can embed {{variables}}
GET requests do not send a body

require_activity.label: Require Follow-up
require_activity.desc: Intercept user actions on the frontend and require a follow-up record before a status change can complete.
require_activity.example:
Trigger: Lead status → Lost
Require reason: Yes
Preset options: No interest, Price too high, Chose another provider
notes: Frontend only; backend API does not validate

require_fields.label: Require Fields
require_fields.desc: Require the user to fill in specified fields before completing an action; cannot proceed if fields are empty.
require_fields.example:
Trigger: Lead status → Confirmed
Required fields: Next Contact Date, Intended Services
notes: Frontend only; backend API does not validate

tipsSection.title: Notes
tipsSection.subtitle: Edge behaviors and security notes when using workflows

actionOrder.title: Action Execution Order
items: Actions within the same workflow run serially in list order
After set_field runs, the new value is immediately available to subsequent template variables
A failing action does not stop subsequent actions (each action has its own try-catch)

emailConfig.title: Email Configuration
items: Uses SendGrid for sending; configure SENDGRID_API_KEY in Cloudflare Workers environment variables
If SENDGRID_API_KEY is not set, send-email actions are silently skipped without error
The sender address is configured by the Worker variable EMAIL_FROM

unmatched.title: Behavior When Variables Don't Match
items: Using a non-existent variable name (e.g. {{xyz}}) keeps {{xyz}} as-is rather than replacing it with an empty string
This makes configuration errors easy to spot and avoids silently sending broken notifications
If a field value is null, the variable is not in the context and referencing it also keeps it as-is

timing.title: Trigger Timing & Frontend Refresh
items: Workflows run asynchronously in the background (fire-and-forget); frontend operations do not wait for completion
set_field writes to the database in real time, but you need to manually refresh the page to see the latest value
require_activity and require_fields only intercept on the frontend; backend API does not validate

webhookSecurity.title: Webhook Security
items: Webhook URLs support template variables; ensure URLs come from trusted sources to avoid SSRF risks
Request signing and HMAC verification are not yet supported; receivers should verify source IP or add a token parameter
Variable substitution in the body happens before sending; sensitive data (e.g. passwords) should not be passed via variables

steps.cloudflare_pages: Create the file below in the project root (not in the build output). If the project has a custom _routes.json, make sure it includes /_t/*. If the build output contains _worker.js (advanced mode), functions/ is ignored; set it up in _worker.js the Cloudflare Workers way instead.
steps.cloudflare_workers:
Add this at the top of the Worker's fetch handler: {{entry}}
and add the forwardToCrm function to the same file. If the Worker serves static assets ([assets] in its config), add run_worker_first = ["/_t/*"] under [assets].
steps.vercel: Create middleware.js (project root; src/middleware.js for Next.js projects using src/). If middleware already exists, merge the matcher and add the /_t/ check at the top of the existing function. Do not create a _t route folder in Next.js (the App Router ignores folders starting with an underscore).
steps.netlify: Create the Edge Function file below. Its config.path already targets /_t/*, so netlify.toml needs no change.
steps.edgeone_pages: Create the Pages Functions file below in the project root (catch-all route; follow the official EdgeOne Pages docs for the file name).
steps.nginx: Add the location below to the website's server { } config (BT Panel: Website → Settings → Config file). Keep the site key in /etc/nginx/crm_site_key.conf. If the site is behind a CDN, replace $remote_addr with the real visitor IP.
steps.php: Create a _t/ directory in the web root with the files below. Nginx + PHP-FPM sites ignore .htaccess; add to the server config instead: location /_t/ { try_files $uri /_t/index.php?$query_string; }. Works for WordPress too.
steps.node: Create crm-proxy.js and mount it early in the Express app: app.use('/_t', crmProxy) (before body parsers such as express.json()). For plain http or other frameworks, follow the comments in the file.

cloudflare_pages.binding:
Cloudflare dashboard → Workers & Pages → website project → Settings:
· Variables and Secrets → add Secret CRM_SITE_KEY = site key
· Bindings → Add → Service binding: variable name CRM, Worker: {{worker}}
Production and Preview are configured separately (at least Production); redeploy afterwards.
cloudflare_pages.url:
Cloudflare dashboard → Workers & Pages → website project → Settings → Variables and Secrets, add two Secrets:
· CRM_SITE_KEY = site key
· CRM_URL = {{origin}} (no trailing /)
Production and Preview are configured separately (at least Production); redeploy afterwards.

cloudflare_workers.binding:
Cloudflare dashboard → Workers & Pages → the website's Worker → Settings:
· Variables and Secrets → add Secret CRM_SITE_KEY = site key
· Bindings → Add → Service binding: variable name CRM, Worker: {{worker}} (or declare it under [[services]] in the wrangler config)
Redeploy afterwards.
cloudflare_workers.url:
Cloudflare dashboard → Workers & Pages → the website's Worker → Settings → Variables and Secrets, add two Secrets:
· CRM_SITE_KEY = site key
· CRM_URL = {{origin}} (no trailing /)
Redeploy afterwards.

vars.vercel:
Vercel project → Settings → Environment Variables, add:
· CRM_SITE_KEY = site key (mark as Sensitive)
· CRM_URL = {{origin}} (no trailing /)
Tick Production (and Preview if needed), then redeploy.
vars.netlify:
Netlify site → Site configuration → Environment variables, add (scope must include Functions):
· CRM_SITE_KEY = site key (mark as secret)
· CRM_URL = {{origin}} (no trailing /)
Redeploy afterwards.
vars.edgeone_pages:
EdgeOne Pages project → Project settings → Environment variables, add:
· CRM_SITE_KEY = site key
· CRM_URL = {{origin}} (no trailing /)
Redeploy afterwards.
vars.nginx:
On the server:
· Create /etc/nginx/crm_site_key.conf containing set $crm_site_key "site key"; (mode 600, outside the web root)
· Make sure the CRM address in the location is {{origin}}
· Run nginx -t && nginx -s reload (BT Panel reloads when you save the config file)
vars.php: On the server, put the site key and the CRM address ({{origin}}) in _t/config.php, or set the environment variables CRM_SITE_KEY and CRM_URL. Make sure config.php is not committed (add it to .gitignore).
vars.node:
Set environment variables on the server, container or process manager (PM2, Docker, etc.):
· CRM_SITE_KEY = site key
· CRM_URL = {{origin}} (no trailing /)
Then restart the service.
vars.other:
On the platform the website actually uses, set on the server side:
· CRM_SITE_KEY = site key
· CRM_URL = {{origin}} (no trailing /)
Only in server-side environment variables or config.

prompt.intro: Please connect this website to the CRM ({{features}}). The website is hosted on: {{platform}}.
prompt.formsIntro: This website already has CRM visitor tracking (the /_t/* proxy and page script are deployed; do not change them). Now only add form lead capture:
prompt.rule: Principle: browsers only call the website's own /_t/*, and the server forwards them to the CRM with the site key. The CRM address and site key must stay on the server (environment variables, encrypted variables or server config files); never put them in front-end code or commit them. Do not change the forwarding logic.
prompt.otherSteps:
First identify the website's tech stack and hosting, and pick a place that can handle /_t/* on the server (edge function, cloud function, reverse proxy or backend route). Implement the proxy protocol below. If the website is static hosting only and cannot handle requests on the server, stop and tell me.

{{spec}}
prompt.script:
Add before </head> on every page: {{scriptTag}}
Once in the shared template or layout is enough; for single-page apps add it to index.html.
prompt.forms:
Make the website's lead forms submit to the same-origin /_t/lead (no key and no CRM URL needed). If the site already has a lead form, adapt it; otherwise build a new one with the fields below, matching the site's design and working well on mobile:
· Native form: action="/_t/lead" method="post"; an optional hidden _redirect field sets the on-site path to go to after success
· Custom frontend: call window.__crmTracker.submitLead(data), use the returned ok to inform the user and show the returned message on failure
· Prevent duplicate submissions: disable the submit button and show "Submitting…" while sending; after success replace the form with a success message instead of showing the form again. The CRM also merges repeat submissions with the same contact within 30 days into the existing lead
· Do not remove the hidden fields the tracking script adds automatically (crm_vid, _hp, _page)
prompt.fields:
· name: full name, required
· phone: mobile number; wechat: WeChat ID; email: email. At least one is required; the CRM uses the first non-empty one as the contact and writes the others to notes
· message: inquiry or message, optional, saved to the lead's notes
· intendedServices: services of interest, optional, multiple allowed. Values must be the service names listed below: native forms use several checkboxes with the same name (or <select multiple>), submitLead takes an array of strings. Values not in the list are recorded as "{{fallback}}" and the original value is written to notes
· Do not add a source field: the source is recorded automatically as the website domain "{{source}}"; the page a visitor submitted from is shown in the CRM visitor journey
· Any other field (e.g. age, city) can be sent under its own name and is written to notes as "field: value"
prompt.services: Available services of interest (from CRM Products & Services; update the form when services are added or removed in the CRM): {{list}}
prompt.servicesNone: There are no services in CRM Products & Services yet, so leave the services field out for now and add it after services are added in the CRM.
prompt.varsTitle: Settings I need to configure in the dashboard or on the server (remind me after the code changes)
prompt.checkTitle: Self-check when done and report back
prompt.check: After deploying, https://<website domain>/_t/t.js should return JavaScript, and POST {"ping":1} (Content-Type: application/json) to /_t/collect and /_t/lead should both return {"data":{"siteId":"..."}}. Then list the files you changed and tell me which dashboard or server settings I still need to configure.
prompt.checkForms: After deploying, POST {"ping":1} (Content-Type: application/json) to /_t/lead should return {"data":{"siteId":"..."}}; then submit a form once with test data and confirm the success message. Finally list the pages you changed.
